title: Famous monarchs and their royal house

house.pick: Which royal house or dynasty did {label} belong to?
house.match: Match each monarch to their royal house.
house.odd: Three of these monarchs belonged to the {value}. Which one didn't?
house.reverse: Which of these monarchs belonged to the {value}?

rows.label: Elizabeth II
rows.description: Queen of the United Kingdom from 1952 to 2022 (1926–2022)
rows.hook: reigned longer than any other British monarch and was famously fond of corgis

rows.label: Harald V of Norway
rows.description: King of Norway from 1991 to 2026 (1937–2026)
rows.hook: competed at several Olympic Games as a sailor before and during his time as a king

rows.label: Victoria
rows.description: Queen of the United Kingdom from 1837 to 1901 (1819-1901)
rows.hook: gave her name to an era and ruled an empire on which the sun never set

rows.label: Henry VIII of England
rows.description: King of England from 1509 to 1547 (1491–1547)
rows.hook: had six wives and broke with the Roman Catholic Church to get his way

rows.label: Napoleon
rows.description: French military leader, French Emperor 1804–1814 and again in 1815 (1769–1821)
rows.hook: rose from a Corsican artillery officer to crown himself emperor before meeting defeat at Waterloo

rows.label: George VI
rows.description: King of the United Kingdom from 1936 to 1952
rows.hook: overcame a stammer to lead his nation through World War II, as shown in The King's Speech

rows.label: Edward VIII
rows.description: King of the United Kingdom in 1936
rows.hook: gave up the throne to marry an American divorcee

rows.label: Elizabeth I of England
rows.description: Queen of England and Ireland from 1558 to 1603 (1533-1603)
rows.hook: was the Virgin Queen who saw off the Spanish Armada

rows.label: Edward VII
rows.description: King of the United Kingdom from 1901 to 1910
rows.hook: waited decades as heir to his mother Queen Victoria and was known for his love of society and racing

rows.label: Alexander the Great
rows.description: king of Macedonia and conqueror of Achaemenid Persia (356–323 BC)
rows.hook: conquered the Persian Empire and is said to have never lost a battle

rows.label: George III of Great Britain
rows.description: King of Great Britain and Ireland from 1760 to 1820 (1738–1820)
rows.hook: lost the American colonies and was said to suffer bouts of madness

rows.label: Mary I
rows.description: Queen of England and Ireland from 1553 to 1558 (1516-1558)
rows.hook: earned the nickname Bloody for burning Protestants and married a Spanish prince

rows.label: William the Conqueror
rows.description: King of England from 1066 to 1087, Duke of Normandy from 1035 to 1087 (1028–1087)
rows.hook: won the Battle of Hastings and ordered the Domesday survey

rows.label: Mary, Queen of Scots
rows.description: Queen of Scotland from 1542 to 1567 (1542–1587)
rows.hook: spent years imprisoned by her cousin Elizabeth I before her execution

rows.label: Charles I of England
rows.description: King of England, Scotland, and Ireland from 1625 to 1649 (1600-1649)
rows.hook: lost a civil war against Parliament and was executed in front of a crowd

rows.label: Henry VII of England
rows.description: King of England from 1485 to 1509
rows.hook: won the Battle of Bosworth Field and founded a new royal dynasty

rows.label: Charlemagne
rows.description: king of Franks, regarded as the first Holy Roman Emperor (747–814) (742-814)
rows.hook: was crowned emperor by the Pope on Christmas Day in Rome

rows.label: Edward VI of England
rows.description: king of England and Ireland from 1547 to 1553
rows.hook: became a boy king at age nine and died in his teens

rows.label: William IV
rows.description: King of the United Kingdom and Hanover from 1830 to 1837
rows.hook: served in the navy and was nicknamed the Sailor King

rows.label: George IV of the United Kingdom
rows.description: King of the United Kingdom and Hanover from 1820 to 1830
rows.hook: was a lavish Regency prince who built the exotic Brighton Pavilion

rows.label: Louis XVI of France
rows.description: King of France and Navarre from 1774 to 1791, then King of the French from 1791 to 1792 (1754-1793)
rows.hook: lost his head to the guillotine during the Revolution and was married to Marie Antoinette

rows.label: Hirohito
rows.description: emperor of Japan from 1926 to 1989
rows.hook: reigned through World War II and announced his nation's surrender by radio

rows.label: Richard III of England
rows.description: king of England from 1483 to 1485
rows.hook: had his skeleton found under a parking lot centuries after dying at Bosworth

rows.label: Puyi
rows.description: Last Emperor of Qing dynasty and Manchukuo (1906–1967)
rows.hook: was crowned as a small child and became the last emperor of China

rows.label: Wilhelm II
rows.description: as King of Prussia last German Emperor from 1888 to 1918 (1859–1941)
rows.hook: was the German kaiser with a withered arm who led his country into World War I

rows.label: Henry V of England
rows.description: King of England from 1413 to 1422
rows.hook: won a famous victory at Agincourt, immortalized by Shakespeare

rows.label: Carl XVI Gustaf of Sweden
rows.description: King of Sweden since 1973
rows.hook: has reigned for decades and presents the Nobel Prizes each year

rows.label: George I of Great Britain
rows.description: King of Great Britain and Ireland from 1714 to 1727
rows.hook: was a German-born king who barely spoke the language of his new subjects

rows.label: George II of Great Britain
rows.description: King of Great Britain and Ireland from 1727 to 1760 (1683-1760)
rows.hook: was the last reigning monarch to personally lead troops in battle

rows.label: Naruhito
rows.description: Emperor of Japan (born 1960)
rows.hook: sits on the Chrysanthemum Throne as the reigning emperor

rows.label: John, King of England
rows.description: King of England from 1199 to 1216
rows.hook: sealed the Magna Carta at Runnymede and is the villain of Robin Hood tales

rows.label: Richard I of England
rows.description: King of England from 1189 to 1199 (1157–1199)
rows.hook: was nicknamed the Lionheart and went off on a crusade

rows.label: Alfred the Great
rows.description: king of Wessex (r. 872–901)
rows.hook: is the legendary ruler said to have burned the cakes while hiding from Viking invaders

rows.label: Abdullah II of Jordan
rows.description: King of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan
rows.hook: is a modern king who once made a cameo appearance on Star Trek

rows.label: Edward I of England
rows.description: King of England from 1272 to 1307
rows.hook: was nicknamed Longshanks and is the villain of the film Braveheart

rows.label: Felipe VI of Spain
rows.description: King of Spain since 2014
rows.hook: carried his country's flag at the Olympic opening ceremony in Barcelona

rows.label: William III of England
rows.description: King of England, Scotland, and Ireland from 1689 to 1702 (1650-1702)
rows.hook: took the throne from his father-in-law in the Glorious Revolution

rows.label: Haile Selassie I
rows.description: Emperor of Ethiopia from 1930 to 1974
rows.hook: is revered as a messiah by followers of the Rastafari movement

rows.label: Edward III of England
rows.description: King of England from 1327 to 1377
rows.hook: started the Hundred Years' War by claiming the French crown

rows.label: Suleiman the Magnificent
rows.description: the tenth and greatest Sultan of Ottoman Empire (1520–1566)
rows.hook: earned the title Lawgiver while his empire reached its greatest power

rows.label: Charles II of Spain
rows.description: king of Spain, lived (1661-1700)
rows.hook: was nicknamed the Bewitched, plagued by ill health linked to generations of inbreeding

rows.label: Akihito
rows.description: Emperor of Japan from 1989 to 2019
rows.hook: was the first emperor in two centuries to step down from the throne while alive

rows.label: Justinian I
rows.description: Eastern Roman Emperor who ruled from 527 to 565 (482-565)
rows.hook: built the Hagia Sophia and had Roman law organized into a famous code

rows.label: Cyrus the Great
rows.description: founder of the Achaemenid Empire (559–529 BC)
rows.hook: freed the exiled Jews from Babylon and built the first great Persian empire

rows.label: Franz Joseph I of Austria
rows.description: Emperor of Austria and King of Hungary (1830-1916)
rows.hook: was the husband of the famous Empress Sisi

rows.label: Henry I of England
rows.description: King of England from 1100 to 1135 (1068–1135)
rows.hook: lost his only legitimate son in the White Ship disaster

rows.label: Ivan the Terrible
rows.description: Tsar of all Russia from 1547 to 1584
rows.hook: was the first ruler crowned tsar and earned a fearsome nickname

rows.label: Kublai Khan
rows.description: founding emperor of the Yuan dynasty, grandson of Genghis Khan (1215–1294)
rows.hook: hosted the Venetian traveler Marco Polo at his court in China

rows.label: Juan Carlos I of Spain
rows.description: King of Spain from 1975 to 2014
rows.hook: helped steer his country back to democracy after a dictator's death

rows.label: Frederick II of Prussia
rows.description: King of Prussia from 1740 to 1786 (1712-1786)
rows.hook: was a flute-playing king who was also a brilliant general

rows.label: Xerxes I
rows.description: fifth Achaemenid emperor (486–465 BC)
rows.hook: was the king who faced 300 Spartans at Thermopylae

rows.label: Akbar
rows.description: the third and greatest Mughal emperor from 1556 to 1605
rows.hook: was known for religious tolerance and built the fortified city of Fatehpur Sikri

rows.label: Philippe of Belgium
rows.description: King of the Belgians since 2013
rows.hook: is the reigning monarch of a country famous for chocolate and waffles

rows.label: Aurangzeb
rows.description: the sixth Mughal Emperor from 1658 to 1707
rows.hook: stretched his empire to its greatest extent and imprisoned his own father

rows.label: Emperor Meiji
rows.description: Emperor of Japan from 1867 until 1912
rows.hook: oversaw a rapid modernization of his country that ended the samurai era

rows.label: Shah Jahan
rows.description: the fifth Mughal Emperor from 1628 to 1658
rows.hook: built the Taj Mahal as a tomb for his beloved wife

rows.label: Babur
rows.description: founder of the Mughal Empire (1526–1530)
rows.hook: swept down from Central Asia to conquer northern India, claiming descent from Timur

rows.label: Beatrix of the Netherlands
rows.description: Queen of the Netherlands from 1980 to 2013 (born 1938)
rows.hook: stepped down so her son could become the first Dutch king in over a century

rows.label: Ashoka
rows.description: Mauryan emperor from 268 to 232 BCE
rows.hook: embraced Buddhism after the carnage of a great war and spread its teachings

rows.label: Louis-Philippe I
rows.description: King of the French from 1830 to 1848 (1773-1850)
rows.hook: was called the Citizen King after coming to power in a July revolution

rows.label: Isabella I of Castile
rows.description: queen of the Crown of Castile, from 1474 to 1504; first queen of a dynastically-united Spain, from 1479 to 1504 (1451–1504)
rows.hook: funded the voyages of an Italian explorer who sailed west in search of Asia

rows.label: Mohammed VI of Morocco
rows.description: king of Morocco since 1999
rows.hook: is the reigning monarch of a North African kingdom that faces the Atlantic and the Mediterranean

rows.label: Mswati III
rows.description: King of Eswatini
rows.hook: is one of the last absolute monarchs in Africa, ruling a small landlocked kingdom

rows.label: Francis II, Holy Roman Emperor
rows.description: also known as Francis I, Emperor of Austria (1768-1835)
rows.hook: dissolved a thousand-year-old European empire after Napoleon's victories, yet kept an imperial crown

rows.label: Charles X of France
rows.description: King of France and Navarre from 1824 to 1830 (1757–1836)
rows.hook: was the last of his line to rule his country, toppled by the July Revolution

rows.label: Alfonso XIII
rows.description: King of Spain from 1886 to 1931 (1886–1941)
rows.hook: lost his throne when republicans won the elections, sending him into exile shortly before a civil war

rows.label: Francis I of France
rows.description: King of France from 1515 to 1547 (1494-1547)
rows.hook: was a Renaissance patron who brought Leonardo da Vinci to his court, and rivaled Charles V

rows.label: Albert II, Prince of Monaco
rows.description: Prince of Monaco (born 1958)
rows.hook: is the reigning head of a tiny Mediterranean principality, and a former Olympic bobsledder

rows.label: Hussein I of Jordan
rows.description: King of Jordan from 1952 to 1999
rows.hook: ruled a desert kingdom for over four decades and made peace with Israel

rows.label: Philip V of Spain
rows.description: King of Spain from 1700 to 1746 (1683–1746)
rows.hook: was the grandson of the Sun King and won a long war over who would inherit a European throne

rows.label: Darius I
rows.description: The fourth and greatest Achaemenid emperor (522–486 BC)
rows.hook: built the Royal Road and ruled a vast empire whose Greek invasion ended at Marathon

rows.label: Chandragupta Maurya
rows.description: founder of the Maurya Empire (350–295 BCE)
rows.hook: united much of the Indian subcontinent after defeating the Nanda kings and Alexander's successors

rows.label: Frederick Barbarossa
rows.description: Holy Roman Emperor from 1155 to 1190
rows.hook: is the red-bearded emperor of legend said to sleep under a mountain, and who drowned on a crusade

rows.label: Philip II of Macedon
rows.description: King of Macedon from 359 to 336 BC
rows.hook: was the father of a famous conqueror and was assassinated at his daughter's wedding

rows.label: Wilhelm I
rows.description: 19th-century German Emperor and King of Prussia (1797–1888)
rows.hook: was proclaimed the first emperor of a unified nation in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles

rows.label: Ferdinand II of Aragon
rows.description: King of Aragon, Sicily, Naples, and Valencia (1452-1516)
rows.hook: married a famous queen, and together they completed the Reconquista and sponsored Columbus

rows.label: Selim I
rows.description: 9th Sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1512 to 1520
rows.hook: nicknamed "the Grim", conquered Egypt and Syria and took the title of caliph

rows.label: Joseph II, Holy Roman Emperor
rows.description: Holy Roman Emperor from 1765 to 1790, (1741-1790).
rows.hook: was an enlightened despot and reformer who is a character in a film about a young composer

rows.label: Philip IV of Spain
rows.description: King of Spain and Portugal (1605-1665)
rows.hook: was the patron of the painter Velázquez and ruled during the Golden Age of the arts

rows.label: Charles VI of France
rows.description: King of France from 1380 to 1422 (1368–1422)
rows.hook: is remembered as "the Mad" after believing his body was made of glass

rows.label: Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck
rows.description: fifth and reigning King of Bhutan
rows.hook: is the young monarch of a Himalayan kingdom famous for measuring Gross National Happiness

rows.label: Frederick II, Holy Roman Emperor
rows.description: King of Sicily, Holy Roman Emperor (1194–1250, 1220–1250)
rows.hook: was nicknamed "Stupor Mundi" and was excommunicated before leading a crusade largely by negotiation

rows.label: Leopold I of Belgium
rows.description: German prince who became the first King of the Belgians (1790–1865)
rows.hook: was a German prince who became the first monarch of a newly independent nation

rows.label: Louis IX of France
rows.description: King of France from 1226 to 1270 (1214–1270)
rows.hook: is the only monarch of his country to be made a saint, after leading two crusades

rows.label: Clovis I
rows.description: first king of the Franks (c. 466-511)
rows.hook: united the Frankish tribes and converted to Catholic Christianity, founding a great medieval kingdom

rows.label: Victor Emmanuel II of Italy
rows.description: King of Sardinia (1849–1861) and King of Italy (1861–1878)
rows.hook: became the first king of a unified peninsula, with the help of Garibaldi and Cavour

rows.label: Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden
rows.description: Swedish king (regent 1611–1632) (1594–1632)
rows.hook: was the "Lion of the North" who led his army to victory in the Thirty Years' War and died at Lützen

rows.label: Louis XII of France
rows.description: King of France from 1498 to 1515
rows.hook: was called the "Father of the People" and fought wars in the Italian peninsula

rows.label: Pedro I of Brazil
rows.description: Emperor of Brazil from 1822 to 1831 and King of Portugal in 1826 (1798-1834)
rows.hook: declared independence from his own father's kingdom with the cry "Independence or Death"

rows.label: Philip IV of France
rows.description: King of France from 1285 to 1314 (1268–1314)
rows.hook: was called "the Fair", crushed the Knights Templar and moved the papacy to Avignon

rows.label: Humayun
rows.description: second Mughal emperor from 1530 to 1540 and 1555 to 1556
rows.hook: lost his throne to Sher Shah Suri but regained it, and left a famed tomb in Delhi

rows.label: Pepin the Short
rows.description: King of the Franks from 751 to 768
rows.hook: was the father of Charlemagne and became the first of a new royal line by deposing the last Merovingian

rows.label: Pedro II of Brazil
rows.description: 2nd and final Emperor of Brazil (r. 1831–89)
rows.hook: was a scholarly ruler who loved science and was overthrown in a military coup, ending the monarchy

rows.label: Christina of Sweden
rows.description: Queen of Sweden, ruled from 1632 until abdication in 1654 (1626–1689)
rows.hook: abdicated, converted to Catholicism and moved to Rome, and was a patron of the philosopher Descartes

rows.label: Charles IV
rows.description: Holy Roman Emperor
rows.hook: issued the Golden Bull and founded the oldest university in central Europe, in Prague

rows.label: Louis the Pious
rows.description: King of the Franks
rows.hook: was the only surviving legitimate son of Charlemagne, whose sons fought over his realm

rows.label: Mu'awiya I
rows.description: founder and first caliph of the Umayyad Caliphate (r. 661–680)
rows.hook: founded the first hereditary line of Islamic rulers, with his capital at Damascus

rows.label: Charles the Bald
rows.description: King of West Francia from 843 to 877 and Carolingian Emperor from 875 to 877
rows.hook: was a grandson of Charlemagne who received the western portion under the Treaty of Verdun

rows.label: Heraclius
rows.description: Byzantine emperor from 610 to 641
rows.hook: defeated the Persians and recovered the True Cross, then lost Egypt and Syria to Arab armies

rows.label: Otto I the Great
rows.description: Holy Roman Emperor from 962 to 973
rows.hook: defeated the Magyars at Lechfeld and was crowned in Rome by the pope in 962

rows.label: Hugh Capet of France
rows.description: King of the Franks
rows.hook: was elected king after the last Carolingian died, founding a line that ruled for centuries

rows.label: Louis XI of France
rows.description: king of France from 1461 to 1483 (1423–1483)
rows.hook: was nicknamed "the Spider King" for his scheming, and outmaneuvered the Duke of Burgundy

rows.label: Vladimir the Great
rows.description: Grand Prince of Kiev
rows.hook: chose Orthodox Christianity for his people and had them baptized in the Dnieper

rows.label: Harun al-Rashid
rows.description: 5th Abbasid caliph (r. 786–809)
rows.hook: is the caliph who ruled from Baghdad's golden age and appears in the tales of the Arabian Nights
